QUIET INTELLIGENCE, USEFUL EVERY DAY

Let small models
do the gardening.

The graph is the shared memory. Models are replaceable helpers. Give each a small, bounded job, and keep every proposed change traceable to its source.

02 / THREE SEEDS WORTH PLANTING

Where should we start?

One foundation. Three useful products.
Choose a direction to explore its first release.

START SMALL, FINISH THE LOOP

One capture. One proposed update. One review.

Start with text and CSV capture, project matching and source-backed update proposals. Add local speech and image models after the review loop works. An eLabFTW adapter would write only approved changes.

FIRST RELEASE: CAPTURE → LINK → REVIEW → EXPORT

OPTIONAL / DEEPER HELP

Your preferred larger model

Explicitly selected for harder questions, with clear control over the context it receives.

eLabFTW ↗

Proposed notebook adapter using its API. Preview and approve writes before sync.

Carpentries Workbench ↗

R-based lesson publishing: a possible destination for curated training material.

R / Shiny + MCP

A proposed interactive analysis and tool layer, inspired by your interest in shinymcp. Adapter details to validate.

Architecture proposal, not shipped integrations. A real local-first version needs a local runtime and model adapters; this hosted concept runs no local or cloud inference.
